solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Tease very loudly after tea

indicators.note: after says the loudness marking comes behind the word for tea

parts.note: CHA is a slang word for tea
FF is fortissimo, the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: Someone is teased noisily over a cup of tea.
explanation.definitionFit: To chaff someone is to banter with them, the same as good-natured teasing.

clue.text: Foreign nobleman and Yankee causing division in England?

parts.note: a count is a continental European noble, equivalent to an earl
Y is Yankee in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A foreign aristocrat and an American stir up discord in England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'division' suggests a quarrel, but here it is an administrative area.
explanation.definitionFit: A county is one of the administrative regions England is divided into, such as Kent or Devon.

clue.text: Trio into a ban might turn out to be this

definitions.text: Trio into a ban might turn out to be this

indicators.note: turn out to be hints that the letters of these words, once rearranged, make something new

explanation.surface: Three people seeking a ban are likely to be opposed to abortion.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: a trio pushing for a ban could be campaigners against abortion.
explanation.definitionFit: Anti-abortion campaigners seek a legal ban on terminating pregnancies, which is what the trio wants.

clue.text: Plumes of smoke finally welcomed by priests

indicators.note: welcomed by puts the letter inside the word for priests

parts.note: Catholic priests are addressed as Father

indicators.note: finally takes the end letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: Clergy greet the last of the smoke rising in plumes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plumes of smoke' looks like one phrase; 'Plumes' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A plume is a large ornamental feather, so plumes are feathers.

clue.text: Show what's on mobile phone? Something to listen with

parts.note: an app is a program installed on a smartphone
you hear with your ear

explanation.surface: A question about a mobile phone feature for listening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Show' looks like a noun for a programme, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To appear is to show up or come into view, the intransitive sense of show.

clue.text: Dark horse seen over eastern hill at coast?

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means placed above, so the horse comes first

parts.note: a dun is a horse of dull greyish-brown colour

explanation.surface: An unexpected contender spotted over an eastern seaside hill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dark horse' suggests an outsider, but it is a horse of dark colouring.
explanation.definitionFit: A dune is a mound of sand heaped by wind, found along beaches.

clue.text: Hard to get inside pen: twist

indicators.note: to get inside places the letter within the word for pen

parts.note: to pen something is to write it
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: It is difficult to get inside a pen, so you squirm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pen' reads as an enclosure, but here it is the verb to write.
explanation.definitionFit: To writhe is to twist and squirm, typically in pain.

clue.text: One no longer beating person offering clarification

parts.note: EX means former, no longer the case
one who beats or batters is a pounder, the word 'One' marking the agent noun

explanation.surface: A former drummer has turned to explaining things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One no longer beating' reads as a single cryptic phrase: an EX-POUNDER is someone who used to pound.
explanation.definitionFit: To expound is to set out and explain in detail, so the person doing it offers clarification.

clue.text: Record being played so behind schedule makes you sad

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
a record being played is on
late means behind schedule

explanation.surface: Playing a record so late in the day leaves you gloomy.
explanation.definitionFit: Disconsolate describes someone downcast who cannot be comforted, a stronger synonym for unhappy.

clue.text: Extremist's quality real, but regularly overlooked

indicators.note: every other letter of these words is passed over, keeping the rest in order

explanation.surface: A fanatic's real nature is routinely missed.
explanation.definitionFit: An ultra is a hardliner holding extreme political views, a synonym for an extremist.

clue.text: Gang in West Side Story film, travelling socialites?

parts.note: the Jets are one of the two rival street gangs in the musical West Side Story
E.T. is the Spielberg film about an extraterrestrial

explanation.surface: A question about a film version of West Side Story and its gang.
explanation.definitionFit: The jet set are wealthy fashionable people who fly between glamorous resorts.

clue.text: Lout starts off yelling on bus

indicators.note: the starting letters of the next three words are taken off and used

explanation.surface: A hooligan shouts on the bus.
explanation.definitionFit: A yob is British slang for a rowdy, uncouth young man, i.e. a lout.

clue.text: Our Phoebe, getting worked up, a possible Brexit supporter?

indicators.note: worked up suggests agitation, so the letters of these words are churned into a new order

explanation.surface: A woman called Phoebe gets angry, and might be a Leave voter.
explanation.definitionFit: A Europhobe dislikes the European Union, so such a person would likely have backed Britain leaving it.

clue.text: Norm making a bow perhaps, and celebrating?

parts.note: par is the standard or norm, as in golf
making a bow in a ribbon or shoelace is one example of tying

explanation.surface: Someone named Norm takes a bow at a celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Norm' poses as a man's name; 'bow' as bending at the waist.
explanation.definitionFit: Partying means having fun at parties, a way of celebrating.

clue.text: Delivers shilling found in small fruit pie

indicators.note: found in places the coin's letter within the pastry word

parts.note: a turnover is a small folded pastry with fruit filling
S is the abbreviation for the old British shilling coin

explanation.surface: Someone delivers a shilling found inside a pie.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn something over to someone is to hand it over, i.e. deliver it.

clue.text: Digits therefore must include megabytes

indicators.note: must include says the first word holds the abbreviation inside it

parts.note: thus means therefore
MB is the abbreviation for megabytes

explanation.surface: Computer data must therefore contain megabytes of numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Digits' suggests numerals in computing, but it means fingers.
explanation.definitionFit: Thumbs are among the digits of the hand, an example of the category.

clue.text: Chucks in five skips

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five
to skip something is to omit it

explanation.surface: Someone throws in five skipping ropes or jumps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chucks' suggests throwing; here it is slang for being sick.
explanation.definitionFit: To chuck (up) is slang for vomiting, so chucks matches vomits.

clue.text: Old coin found in tart, not the last

indicators.note: not the last says the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: tart in taste means sour

explanation.surface: An antique coin turns up inside a pastry tart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tart' looks like the pastry, but it is the adjective meaning sharp-tasting.
explanation.definitionFit: The sou was a French coin of small value, no longer in circulation.

clue.text: Positive aspect is due to reform, quietly included

indicators.note: included puts the quiet letter inside the reshaped letters
to reform is to reshape, so these letters are put in a new order

parts.note: P is piano, the musical marking for quiet

explanation.surface: An upside to a reform that is due, quietly brought in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to reform' turns IS DUE into USIDE, with P set inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An upside is the favourable side of a situation, its good point.

clue.text: Consistently, college class lazy in the extreme

parts.note: UNI is short for university, a college
a form is a class in a British school

indicators.note: only the extreme letters, first and last, of the word are kept

explanation.surface: A university class is lazy through and through.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something uniformly means doing it the same way every time, without variation.

clue.text: Work beginning for office: drink up!

indicators.note: beginning for takes the starting letter of the following word
in a down clue, up says the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: An office party starts with a call to drink up.
explanation.definitionFit: An opus is a creative work, especially a numbered musical composition.

clue.text: Asian artist and queen visiting India twice

indicators.note: visiting puts the artist and queen inside the pair of letters
twice says the India letter is used a second time, so there is one each side

parts.note: I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
Q is the chess and card abbreviation for queen

explanation.surface: A painter and a queen pay two visits to India.
explanation.definitionFit: An Iraqi comes from Iraq, a country in western Asia.

clue.text: Ban a stunt that's recreated a feature of apartheid

indicators.note: recreated means made again in a different form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A daredevil stunt is banned and then staged again.
explanation.definitionFit: Bantustans were nominally self-governing homelands for black South Africans under the apartheid regime.

clue.text: Fools back in diocese, egotistical

indicators.note: back says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters sit inside the run of the next two words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Idiots in the diocese are full of themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks the run of letters inside 'diocese, egotistical'; 'back' reverses them.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone a goose means they are silly, so geese is a plural for fools.
